problem: The Required website browser lane could remain in progress because standalone visibility verification contained an unbounded document.fonts.ready wait and overly expensive retry envelopes across the full sitemap.
root_cause: The browser verifier relied on a job-level timeout but did not bound every asynchronous wait inside the route loop. A single unresolved browser promise could consume the runner until the outer job timeout.
fix: Bound document.fonts.ready with a deterministic timeout
Reduce navigation retries and navigation timeout
Add a total fail-closed sweep budget
Preserve product assertions while preventing runner leaks
Make expensive PR workflows single-flight per PR so a new head cancels superseded queued/in-progress work
Bound expensive specialist jobs with explicit job timeouts
Mirror specialist PR path scopes onto main push triggers so unrelated merges do not fan out specialist CI
Replace run-id concurrency keys with stable ref/PR keys where supersession is intended
Register newly introduced delivery skills in the canonical System Map in the same lineage
Migrate stale pricing regressions to semantic content-addressed cache and dataset-readiness invariants
Restore content-growth-ci push.branches=[main] and keep main out of paths
Run independent viewport sweeps in bounded parallel batches so the full production sitemap readback can complete inside its fail-closed budget
Make visibility concurrency regressions assert semantic coverage and bounded worker structure rather than one obsolete loop implementation
Size production route concurrency to the observed 93-route sitemap: 8 route workers per viewport × 3 bounded viewport workers while retaining the 8-minute fail-closed sweep budget
prevention_rule: Every browser/readback or expensive CI workflow must bound async waits and total runtime, use stable supersession keys, scope specialist main triggers to owned paths, validate YAML semantics after automated rewrites, and size explicit route × viewport worker budgets to route inventory without weakening fail-closed assertions.

invariants: each navigation attempt has a finite timeout
page-side font readiness has a finite timeout
sitemap retrieval has a finite timeout
the full visibility sweep has a total fail-closed runtime budget
public-page visibility, occlusion, content-length and CLS assertions remain enforced

failed_approaches: A generic text transformation assumed push.branches was a one-line YAML scalar and inserted paths before a multi-line branch list, producing an invalid semantic structure even though the file remained textually plausible.
A regression migration attempt changed the runtime contract but left older tests hard-coded to a timestamp cache key, literal selector spelling, and a stale System Map inventory.
A workflow rewrite left content-growth-ci.yml with an empty push.branches key and moved main into paths, creating semantic YAML drift that only the multiline branch-scope regression exposed.

Route-level concurrency alone was insufficient because phone, tablet and desktop sweeps still executed sequentially; the phone sweep could consume the entire 8-minute global budget before tablet/desktop started.
A stale regression asserted the exact sequential viewport loop syntax instead of the intended invariant of complete route × viewport coverage under bounded concurrency.
With 93 public routes, 4 route workers per viewport still exceeded the 480-second production sweep budget even after viewport-level parallelism.
